title: User preferences: the person's standing choices
description: Lives in the user directory (default ~/.lattice/preferences.json, LATTICE_PREFERENCES to move it). Distinct from the assembly overlay beside it: an overlay says what is ASSEMBLED and is written by installs; this says how the person likes it SET. The difference is why it exists — a setting recovered from a conversation's ledger would only come back in that conversation, and a standing choice has to hold in a conversation that did not exist yet when it was made. Precedence, strongest first: an environment variable typed on THIS launch, then this file, then the built-in default; something said a second ago outranks something chosen last week. Nothing here is load-bearing: a missing, unreadable or malformed document reads as empty rather than stopping startup.

thinking.description: How hard the main model thinks. A rung of Lattice's neutral ladder, which each dialect translates to its own wire (a word on one, a token budget on another) so the same setting means the same thing across providers. `false` = off. A string off the ladder is passed to the provider untouched — the escape hatch for a provider-specific value. Omitted entirely = say nothing at all in the request, which is not the same as off, and is the only safe setting for an endpoint that rejects unknown parameters.

model.description: Which entry of the model catalog (schemas/model_catalog.json) to run, by its short name — the name rather than the model id, so the choice survives an entry being pointed at a newer model. A name the catalog no longer has is ignored rather than fatal: deleting an entry gets the default back, not a program that will not start.

additionalProperties.description: Preferences this version does not know. Kept on write rather than dropped: one document, and a command that sets one key must not delete a choice it knows nothing about.
